result.title: FlowCF: Sparse Counterfactual Explanations for Mixed-Type Tabular Data using Flow Matching
result.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Geometric Distributional Deep Learning (GDDL) Workshop
result.summary: In the field of Explainable AI (XAI), counterfactual (CF) explanations interpret a model's decision by suggesting the changes to the input that would lead to a more favourable outcome. To be useful in practice, such an explanation should change few features and change them as little as possible, properties known as sparsity and proximity. We observe that existing methods remain limited in this respect, especially for numerical features, whether they are model-agnostic and amortised, or gradient-based with full access to the model. In this paper, we propose FlowCF, a model-agnostic generative method that frames CF generation as sparse transport from the factual to the target class. We solve this transport with flow matching, which we extend to mixed feature types with a novel mixed flow operator, and exploit the resulting geometry to optimise for sparsity through a gating network that minimises the number of features the transport changes. Extensive experiments on six benchmark datasets demonstrate that FlowCF produces the best numerical sparsity and proximity, changing 29% of the numerical features where the best baseline changes 89%, at 70% smaller displacement, while remaining comparable on the other desiderata.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 FlowCF，把反事实解释生成视为从原始样本到目标类别的稀疏传输问题，用 flow matching 结合混合类型流动算子与门控网络来最小化被改动的特征数，在六个表格基准上取得更好的稀疏性与接近度。
AI.relevance_reason: 反事实的稀疏门控与「最小改动即解释」概念，可能启发 LVR 中对 latent 状态改动幅度、证据筛选与停止决策的度量方式，需核查其稀疏传输几何是否能迁移为 latent 轨迹的稀疏性约束。
